summary: READ-ONLY check of the webhook base URL fixes in PREVIEW (live Vapi, no saves or other changes). All 4 requested items pass. Settings webhook_base_url equals the preview origin, so no mismatch warning shows on load. Typing https://example.org makes the amber webhook-mismatch-warning appear with correct text. Clicking use-this-site-url-btn fills the field with the preview origin and the warning disappears. The origin with a trailing '/' also shows no warning. After a reload the stored value is unchanged (still the preview origin), which confirms nothing was saved; the only POSTs during the run were CDN/analytics beacons, none to the app's API. The export Recording links all start with https://identity-check-ops.preview.emergentagent.com/api/recordings/ and a link returns 200 audio/wav. Sending a spoofed X-Forwarded-Host through the public ingress had no effect (the ingress overwrites it). Settings regression: pronunciation editor, script templates (script-hi-IN-reverify), reset-scripts-btn (not clicked) and the voice profiles table with a voice-*-tts_provider column for en-IN, bn-IN and hi-IN all render. Production was not touched.
action_items: PROD still needs the user/admin to open PROD /rpi/settings, click 'Use this site's URL' (or clear the field) and Save, so that PROD webhook_base_url points to PROD. This was not verified here (the run was read-only and production was off limits).
critical_code_review_comments: public_base() trusts x-forwarded-host/host whenever it is not localhost. This is safe behind the current ingress (a spoofed header was overwritten), but a direct backend hit with a crafted Host header could put arbitrary hosts in the CSV links. Consider an allowlist (e.g. PUBLIC_BASE_URL/webhook_base_url hosts).
The playbook asks for a 'Jev route' check, but the app has no such route (no 'jev' found in server.py), so it was not applicable.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live Vapi mode: stay read-only. Campaign 6ad2faad17b693b316bc636b has completed calls with recordings. test_webhook_base_readonly.py is safe to rerun. The remaining open item is the PROD webhook_base_url fix, which a user must save in PROD.
